speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the rash first appeared and if it started on your trunk before spreading to your extremities? Also, have you noticed any joint pain or swollen lymph nodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the facial rash sparing the perioral area is quite characteristic. I'd like to check if the rash on her arms and legs looks like flat, red patches that are spreading outward. Also, has she had any exposure to someone with a similar illness recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS. The requested Measles IgM antibody test results and the patient's immunization history (specifically for the MMR vaccine) are not available in the current data. Clinical observations include a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, and a facial rash sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of joint pain and respiratory distress is helpful. The clinical picture of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a trunk rash, preceded by fever and rhinorrhea, is highly suggestive. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
